cards.explanation: The answer is the wine. "When the wine ran out…" is how the writer puts it. I think a wedding running out of wine is a rough spot, friends, and I've had a cookie jar echo at me before. Sad sound.
The answer is Jesus' mother. She says to Him, "They have no more wine." She brings it straight to Him, friends. Short and simple, no speech needed.

The answer is that she tells the servants to do whatever He says. She turns to them and says, "Do whatever He tells you." Jesus has just said His hour hasn't come yet, and she still points the servants to Him. I think that's some serious trust, friends.

The answer is to fill them with water. Jesus tells the servants, "Fill the jars with water." Those six stone jars had been set there for the Jewish rites of purification, and each could hold from twenty to thirty gallons (John 2:6). So the servants had a lot of filling to do, bakers, and they filled them to the brim.
The answer is False. The text says, "So they filled them to the brim." Six jars, friends, each able to hold from twenty to thirty gallons, all filled to the top.
The answer is False. The master of the banquet "…did not know where it was from…" He just tastes it and gets to be impressed, friends. The text says the servants who had drawn the water knew.
The answer is servants. The text says "…the servants who had drawn the water knew." They drew the water, and they knew where it was from, bakers. I'd love to have seen their faces.

The answer is that he saved the fine wine until now. The master of the banquet says, "But you have saved the fine wine until now!" Everyone else brings out the good stuff first, friends. He sounds shocked, and I would be too if my last cookie tasted better than my first.
The answer is True. The text says Jesus revealed His glory, "…and His disciples believed in Him." This is called the first of His signs, friends. Their belief is right there in the verse.
The answer is Capernaum. After this, Jesus went down to Capernaum with His mother and brothers and His disciples, and they stayed a few days. Quite a crowd for a short visit, bakers.
